title: A.R. Rahman Called Sonu Nigam Back to the Studio. The Song Is for Aamir Khan's Partition Epic.
excerpt: Batwara 1947 reunites Sunny Deol with the director who made him a star, drops on Independence Day, and now has the most romantic voice in Hindi cinema singing a melody written by Javed Akhtar.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • A.R. Rahman collaborates with Sonu Nigam for the song 'Oh Tabassum' in Batwara 1947.
  • Batwara 1947 marks a reunion of director Rajkumar Santoshi and actor Sunny Deol after nearly 30 years.
  • The film adapts a banned play about the 1947 Partition, focusing on displacement and identity.
  • Batwara 1947 releases on August 14, 2026, coinciding with India's Independence Day.
  • The film features a star-studded cast, including Preity Zinta and Shabana Azmi.
A Star-Studded Reunion
›Director: Rajkumar Santoshi
›Actor: Sunny Deol
›Previous Collaborations: Ghayal, Damini, Ghatak
›Time Since Last Film Together: Nearly 30 years
There are collaborations, and then there is **A.R. Rahman** posting a studio selfie with **Sonu Nigam** and writing, with genuine wonder: *"Bro… how can you sound so Romantic?"* https://youtube.com/watch?v=DstkbSnWFf4 ![Aamir Khan — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/65/Aamir_Khan_at_the_success_bash_of_Secret_Superstar.jpg) That's the energy behind **'Oh Tabassum'**, a new melody from **Batwara 1947** — the Partition drama produced by **Aamir Khan Productions** that's been building quietly into one of the most anticipated releases of the year. Rahman announced on social media that Nigam had come in to record the track, composed by Rahman himself with lyrics by **Javed Akhtar**, and something about the pairing just landed. Two of Indian music's most decorated voices, back in the same room, for a film about the most seismic event in the subcontinent's modern history. ## The Film That Took Three Decades to Happen > **"Bro… how can you sound so Romantic?" — A.R."** Directed by **Rajkumar Santoshi**, Batwara 1947 marks a reunion that Bollywood has waited nearly thirty years for. Santoshi and **Sunny Deol** together gave us **Ghayal**, **Damini**, and **Ghatak** — films that defined an entire era of Hindi cinema's angry-young-man archetype. The director-actor pairing was once considered Bollywood's most reliable blockbuster machine. Now they're back, and the stakes couldn't be higher. The film is based on **Asghar Wajahat's** acclaimed play *Jis Lahore Nai Vekhya, O Jamya E Nai* — a Punjabi proverb that roughly translates to "if you haven't seen Lahore, you haven't truly lived." The theatrical production has reportedly remained banned in Pakistan, and this is its first adaptation for the screen. Set against the upheaval of 1947, it follows the lives of millions displaced by Partition, forced to abandon everything and start over. ![Sonu Nigam — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/76/Sonu_Nigam123.jpg) ## A Cast Built for Prestige The ensemble reads like a roll call of Indian cinema's finest. **Preity Zinta** returns to the screen in what promises to be a substantial role — her pairing with Sunny Deol carries an instant nostalgia for fans who remember their chemistry in the original **Gadar**. **Shabana Azmi** brings the kind of gravitas that elevates any frame she occupies. **Ali Fazal**, fresh off international projects, adds a contemporary edge to the period setting. **Karan Deol** joins his father on screen, making it a rare Deol family affair. The technical team matches the ambition. **Santosh Sivan** — the man who shot **Dil Se** and **Before the Rains** — handles the cinematography, practically guaranteeing that the Partition landscape will be rendered with the kind of visual poetry the subject demands. ## Why the Diaspora Should Be Paying Attention ![Rajkumar Santoshi — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e2/Rajkumar_Santoshi_%28cropped%29.jpg)
The Impact of Partition
›Film Adaptation of Banned Play: Jis Lahore Nai Vekhya, O Jamya E Nai
›Focus on Displacement and Identity
›Significance for NRI Families
Partition stories hit differently when you're living abroad. The displacement, the rebuilding, the identity questions — these aren't abstract history for NRI families. They're dinner-table conversations. They're the reason your grandparents still get quiet sometimes. Batwara 1947 releases on **August 14, 2026** — the eve of Independence Day — in a move that's both commercially savvy and emotionally loaded. For Indian audiences in the US, UK, and Canada, this is the kind of film that fills diaspora theatres on opening weekend: a prestige period drama with star power, a composer who won an Oscar, and a story that lives in the collective memory of every South Asian family. Rahman and Akhtar together have produced some of Hindi cinema's most enduring songs. Adding Sonu Nigam — whose voice carries an ache that few can replicate — to a Partition love ballad called 'Oh Tabassum' feels almost unfairly stacked. If the song is even half as good as that studio energy suggests, it could be the romantic anthem of the year.
Release Date and Distribution
›Release Date: August 14, 2026
›Coincides with India's Independence Day
›Produced by Aamir Khan Productions
›Distributed by PVR Inox Pictures
> "Thrilled to have Sonu Nigam back in our studios to sing Oh Tabassum melody from the movie Batwara 1947. Written by Javed Akhtar. Directed by Rajkumar Santoshi and produced by Aamir Khan. Bro… how can you sound so Romantic?" — A.R. Rahman The film is produced by Aamir Khan and **Aparna Purohit** under the Aamir Khan Productions banner and will be distributed by **PVR Inox Pictures** for a worldwide theatrical release. Mark August 14. This one's going to matter.
